scalesUsed.application: Core melodic framework for the vocal chant and guitar riffs

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G# - A - B - C# - D - E
scalesUsed.application: The use of the D chord (bVII) suggests a mixolydian flavor common in rock music

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Mixolydian-influenced with the bVII (D) chord lending a raw, bluesy rock feel
keyAndScale.keySignature: 4 sharps (F#, C#, G#, D#) in strict E major, but the D natural in D chord gives mixolydian color
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C# minor is the relative minor of E major

mainProgression.description: A raw, powerful three-chord riff that defines garage rock. The E to D movement creates the mixolydian character, while A provides the subdominant lift.

sectionProgressions.description: The repeating four-chord riff that drives the entire song, played with aggressive strumming and raw energy
Same chord progression as the verse but with the iconic 'G-L-O-R-I-A' vocal chant over the top
Sections where the band vamps on the E chord, building tension before releasing into the full riff

harmonicFunction: E (I) - Tonic chord and the home base, played with aggressive open strumming
D (bVII) - Flatted seventh chord creating the mixolydian rock sound and forward motion
A (IV) - Subdominant chord providing harmonic lift before resolving back to E

techniques.name: Three-Chord Garage Rock Riff
techniques.description: The driving E-D-A riff pattern that became the template for garage rock, played with raw, aggressive downstrokes

notes: E: 0-2-2-1-0-0 (open E major chord)
D: X-X-0-2-3-2 (open D major chord)
A: X-0-2-2-2-0 (open A major chord)
Each chord gets two beats in the main riff pattern
The riff repeats throughout the entire song with no variation needed
sequence: Learn the three open chord shapes: E, D, and A
Practice the riff pattern: E (2 beats) - D (2 beats) - A (2 beats) - E (2 beats)
Use strong, confident downstrokes on every strum
Build up to 132 BPM with steady timing
tips: This song is all about attitude - play with energy and confidence
Keep your strumming aggressive with mostly downstrokes
Do not overthink the chord changes - keep it simple and raw
The D chord transition from E is the trickiest - practice it in isolation

techniques.name: Rhythmic Chanting Build-Up
techniques.description: The technique of vamping on a single chord while building intensity, then releasing into the full riff with the vocal chant

notes: Vamp on the open E chord with steady eighth-note strumming
Gradually increase strumming intensity and volume
The build creates tension that releases when the D and A chords enter
This dynamic contrast is central to the song's excitement
sequence: Start strumming the E chord quietly with light eighth notes
Gradually increase volume and attack over 4-8 bars
Launch into the full E-D-A riff at peak intensity
Maintain high energy through the chorus chant
tips: Think of the build-up as going from a whisper to a shout
The contrast between quiet and loud is what makes this song exciting
Practice controlling your strumming dynamics from soft to loud
Time the peak of the build to coincide with the vocal entry
details.progression: E (vamp) building to E - D - A full riff

sections.name: Intro / Verse
sections.description: The song opens with the hypnotic E chord vamp before launching into the three-chord riff with Van Morrison's spoken-word verses
notes: Start with the E chord vamp building intensity
Launch into the three-chord riff when the band comes in fully
Keep the strumming driving and rhythmic throughout
The verse is essentially the same riff repeating under the vocals

sections.name: Chorus (G-L-O-R-I-A Chant)
sections.description: The iconic spelling chant 'G-L-O-R-I-A' sung over the same three-chord riff with maximum energy
notes: Same chord progression as verse but with full band intensity
The chant the iconic vocal hook drives the energy to its peak
Strum with maximum power and confidence during the chorus
Each letter of the chant aligns with the strumming rhythm

sections.name: Verse 2 / Build-Up
sections.description: Second verse returns to the E chord vamp and spoken vocals before building back to the chorus
notes: Dynamics drop back down for the verse
Build intensity gradually through the verse
The E chord vamp sections allow for dynamic contrast
Drive toward the chorus with increasing volume

sections.name: Final Chorus / Outro
sections.description: Extended final chorus with repeated G-L-O-R-I-A chant building to the explosive ending
notes: Maximum energy throughout the final chorus
The chant repeats with building intensity
Keep the riff driving and consistent to the end
Final resolution on a big, sustained E chord

guitar.recommended: Fender Telecaster or any solid-body electric guitar
alternatives: Any electric guitar with single-coil or humbucker pickups
guitar.pickup: Bridge pickup for bright, aggressive tone

amp.recommended: Fender Bassman or Vox AC30 (cranked for natural overdrive)
alternatives: Any tube amp with natural breakup

effects.distortion: None needed - use amp overdrive from cranked volume
effects.reverb: Light spring reverb from the amp
effects.other: No pedals needed. Raw, cranked amp tone is the authentic garage rock sound.

beginner.focus: Learn the three chord shapes and the basic riff pattern
steps: Learn open E, D, and A chord shapes individually
Practice switching between E and D (the most important transition)
Practice the riff pattern: E - D - A - E at slow tempo

intermediate.focus: Add dynamics, energy, and play through the full song
steps: Build up to 132 BPM with the full riff pattern
Add dynamic variation between quiet verses and loud choruses
Play through the entire song structure without stopping

advanced.focus: Perform with attitude, sing along, and add lead embellishments
steps: Sing the G-L-O-R-I-A chant while strumming the riff
Add blues scale embellishments between chord changes
Experiment with power chord versions (E5, D5, A5) for heavier sound
Practice performing with a band or backing track

commonMistakes: Playing too cleanly - this song should sound raw and energetic
Losing the tempo when switching between E and D chords
Not enough dynamic contrast between verse build-ups and chorus
Overcomplicating the strumming - keep it simple with driving downstrokes
practiceRoutine: Warm up with E, D, A chord switches for 3 minutes
Practice the riff pattern at 100 BPM for 3 minutes
Build tempo up to 132 BPM gradually over several passes
Work on dynamics: play the E vamp softly, then explode into the full riff
Play through the entire song from start to finish
focusAreas: Clean transitions between E, D, and A chords
Dynamic control from soft builds to loud releases
metronomeWork: Start at 90 BPM with the three-chord riff pattern
Increase by 10 BPM until reaching 132 BPM
Practice the E chord vamp at various tempos to build timing
Use the metronome on beats 2 and 4 for a rock backbeat feel
